newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Gurkhas troops happy to take families to UK.
newsitem.headline: HK Gurkhas troops happy to take families to UK.

text.p: Gurkha soldiers based in Hong Kong on Tuesday welcomed their newly granted right to bring their families with them when they are rebased in Britain.
"I think it's jolly good news for us," said captain Nvindra Bikram Gurung of the Queen's Gurkha Signals.
"It's been announced we're getting family permission in the U.K., so all the boys are happy and their families are happy," he told reporters.
Gurkha officers and senior non-commissioned officers from Nepal serving in the British garrison in Hong Kong can have their families with them on a permanent basis.
Sergeants and junior soldiers receive "family permission" for at least three years during their first 15 years of service.
Such "accompanied service" had not been permitted in Britain.

But taking advantage of the drawdown of the Hong Kong garrison ahead of the colony's handover to China in midnight June 30, the British army undertook its first major review in 40 years of Gurkha terms of service to improve the troops' pay and conditions.
"These improvements are much to be welcomed," said Major General Bryan Dutton, Commander British Forces Hong Kong.

"They will correct anomalies which have developed over the years in the Gurkhas' terms and conditions of service. They are an appropriate and thoroughly justified response to the loyalty shown by all Gurkhas during a particularly difficult period."
In addition to the question of families, all Gurkha soldiers in the British army, wherever they are serving, will have their take-home pay raised to the same level as their British counterparts.
They will also be able to either send their children to British schools or get education allowances back home.
The Gurkhas -- Nepali soldiers renowned for their hardiness, loyalty and combat skills -- have served with the British army for 180 years.
At one time about 3,000 Gurkhas served in Hong Kong. Now only about 100 remain.
